name: Quivver → BTB — v2 (Looped Runway)
description: Using loops to extend the coexistence window. Quivver's last 8 bars (kick/bass loop, no melody, 1A) looped 4x = 32 bars of rhythmic runway. BTB's first 8 bars (pure kick in 1A) looped 3x = 24 bars of intro runway. This creates a ~40 bar overlap where both tracks play their looped rhythmic content without harmonic clash.

tracks.name: Quivver — Brothers & Sisters (Original Mix)
tracks.notes: LUFS -14.2. cue_out at 226 (melody end). Loop last 8 bars (218-226) x4 = 32 bars of kick/bass runway. These bars are a steady -9.2dB kick/bass loop with no melodic content.

tracks.name: Below The Belt (Chris Micali Remix)
tracks.notes: LUFS -13.9. cue_in at 0 (using kick intro). Loop first 8 bars x3 = 24 bars of pure kick in 1A before the track develops.

transitions.notes: v2: 40-bar overlap across looped sections. Both tracks playing their non-melodic, 1A-compatible rhythmic loops. Gradual crossfade — the kicks should coexist since both are repetitive patterns. The loops create the extended runway that a DJ would use to ride both decks.
